analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses against the replayed BASE/HEAD stop-matching source, submission patch, and all three submodule pointer changes. No concrete security regression is independently established in the visible changes.

EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249-250 forwards stopStringScope into request translation. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift:14-31 uses that scope when reconstructing the stop responsible for termination; the unscoped earliest-match behavior is unchanged. These changes concern output-channel integrity and generation termination (A-001, TB-007), with potential availability/cancellation interactions (A-018, T-010). They do not visibly change authorization, attestation, hop encryption, billing, or encrypted cache policy. Scope-aware stopping alone does not demonstrate analysis-channel disclosure or weakened cache isolation.

Material uncertainties remain. The implementations behind the new pins in libs/mlx:1, libs/mlx-swift:1 and libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 were not supplied. Review their deltas and the request translation/scope-selection contract to establish that incremental stopping and whole-text replay agree, including split Harmony markers, and that StopHoldback.scan.text preserves the raw-prefix scalar count assumed at StopSequence.swift:30. Verify bounded generation, output-channel filtering and token accounting remain correct. Under T-041, confirm the translation/dependency changes preserve independent coordinator-authored cacheScope/cacheSalt binding and compatible checkpoint reuse; no weakening is shown here.

The replay is incomplete (four units omitted), so prior claims about submission admission/cleanup and documentation context cannot all be independently rechecked. Dependency and scope-contract review is required before clearing the combined change; missing implementations are coverage limits, not evidence of missing controls.
